title: 👑 Elite Challenge: Modal Mastery Under Pressure

questions.prompt: Find the error: one of these sentences contains a mistake. Which one?

options.text: She has to wear a uniform.
We will have to leave early.
They had to move to Sfax.

questions.explanation: "He musts respect the rules" is the sentence with the mistake: "must" never changes, whatever the subject, so it is "He must respect the rules" (or "He has to respect the rules"). "has to" with she, "will have to" for the future and "had to" for the past are all correct.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the same meaning as "It is a good thing for you to eat more fruit."?

options.text: You ought to eat more fruit.
You are able to eat more fruit.

questions.explanation: "A good thing to do" is advice, and "ought to" + base verb gives advice, like "should": you ought to eat more fruit. "mustn't" forbids it, "might" only says it is possible, and "are able to" talks about ability, not about what is good for you.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Last year Rania's father found a job in Sousse, so the family ___ move. Next year she ___ take the national exam."
questions.explanation: The first obligation is in the past (last year) → "had to"; the second is in the future (next year) → "will have to": the family had to move, she will have to take the exam. After "will" the verb stays bare, so "will has to" is wrong; "must" has no past and no future form; "have to" is the present.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sentences expresses the same function?

options.text: You shouldn't litter. / You mustn't litter.
It might rain. / You must go.

questions.explanation: "Don't" + base verb and "mustn't" + base verb both express prohibition, so "Don't litter! / You mustn't litter." is the pair with one function. The trap is "shouldn't / mustn't": "shouldn't" is advice (a choice), "mustn't" is prohibition. "can't" is inability against a prohibition, and "might" is possibility against an obligation.

options.text: My sisters is able to cook couscous.
My sisters can to cook couscous.
My sisters are able to cooking couscous.
My sisters are able to cook couscous.

questions.explanation: "Be able to" + base verb, with "be" agreeing with the subject: "my sisters" is they → "are able to cook". The subject decides "be", so "is" is wrong; "can" never takes "to"; and after "able to" the verb stays bare, never -ing.

questions.prompt: A doctor explains: "Smoking ___ damage your lungs, so you ___ smoke." Which pair completes the sentence correctly?
questions.explanation: Damage is possible, not certain → "may" (perhaps); the doctor then advises against smoking → "shouldn't": smoking may damage your lungs, so you shouldn't smoke. "may / should" contradicts itself by advising to smoke, "should to" wrongly adds "to", and "must / may" turns the damage into an obligation.
